newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan beer makers post mixed earnings for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan beer makers post mixed earnings for 1996.

text.p: Japan's top beer makers on Thursday unveiled mixed results for 1996, with longtime leader Kirin Brewery Co Ltd suffering a steep slide in profits due to sluggish sales of its mainstay brands.
Kirin's parent current profit slid by 30 percent to 52.8 billion yen ($425 million) in 1996 and its sales also dipped 3.5 percent to 1.3 trillion yen ($10.4 billion).

The lacklustre sales of Kirin brand beers -- Lager and Ichibanshibori -- allowed the number-two Asahi Breweries Ltd to raise the sales of its flagship Super Dry brand, helping make Asahi to post a healthy profit increase last year.
Asahi's parent current profit increased 18 percent to total 25.7 billion yen ($207 million) in 1996 with a 7.0 percent rise in sales to 931.2 billion yen ($7.50 billion).
Third-ranked Sapporo Breweries Ltd posted a two percent rise in its profits to 14.6 billion yen ($117 million) with sales almost flat at 619.8 billion yen ($4.99 billion).
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
Kirin saw tough roads ahead, although it forecast better profits for this calendar year.
"We cannot expect any rapid growth in total beer demand from now on, and we believe competition among beer makers will further intensify this year," Kirin said in a statement.

Kirin predicted its parent current profit will grow 20 percent in 1997 to 63 billion yen ($508 million). Asahi predicted a 17 percent rise in the current profit to 30 billion yen ($241 million). Sapporo expected a 6.4 percent rise to 15.5 billion yen ($125 million).
In January, Kirin scored an embarrassing defeat by falling behind Asahi in shipments for the first time in 44 years.
Asahi captured a 38.3 percent domestic share and Kirin a close 37.2 percent among the top four Japanese beer makers.
Sapporo's share was 19.0 percent while Suntory Ltd trailed with 5.6 percent.
Asahi's rise to the top was largely due to a robust 42 percent year-on-year rise in sales of its "Super Dry" beer.
Some analysts said Kirin's sluggish sales were largely due to a mistake in its marketing strategy.

Kirin had redirected its marketing efforts toward mass retailers at the expense of its traditional base of local liquor shops, but the move allowed Asahi to chip away at Kirin's share of sales by small retailers, they said.
Analysts expect competition in the beer market to keep bubbling as the top four battle for market share amid flat demand. They saw little room for the mature market to grow.

"Kirin continues to flounder and has added the embarrassment of beginning the year behind Asahi in market share. We're not optimistic on the power to reverse the declining trend," Patricia Horvath, a financial analyst at UBS Securities Ltd, said in a recent commentary. ($1=124 yen)
